course_name_original: Mercados y Regulación del Sector Energético
prerequisites: Basic general and transversal knowledge and competencies in engineering, such as those acquired after completing a Bachelor's degree in industrial engineering, mining engineering, or civil engineering.

learning_outcomes.text: Possess and understand knowledge that provides a basis or opportunity to be original in the development and/or application of ideas, often in a research context.
Students should be able to apply acquired knowledge and problem-solving skills in new or unfamiliar environments within broader (or multidisciplinary) contexts related to their field of study.

Students should be able to integrate knowledge and deal with the complexity of making judgments based on information that, being incomplete or limited, includes reflections on the social and ethical responsibilities linked to the application of their knowledge and judgments.
Students should be able to communicate their conclusions and the ultimate knowledge and reasons that support them to specialized and non-specialized audiences clearly and unambiguously.
Students should possess learning skills that allow them to continue studying in a way that will be largely self-directed or autonomous.
Problem-solving in new or unfamiliar environments within multidisciplinary contexts related to energy engineering.
Ability to integrate knowledge to formulate applications for the development of new energy technologies.
Autonomous learning ability that allows continuing to study by searching and assimilating specialized documentation in scientific-technical literature.

Ability for the study, proposal, and application of different types of technologies to improve the use and energy efficiency of installations or plants, comparing alternatives by performance and costs.
Assessment and application of advanced technologies for thermoelectric generation with minimum pollutant emissions.
Understand how energy supply markets operate and evolve.
Perform demand analysis and cost estimations for energy installations.
Understand the effects of regulatory strategies on energy markets.
Perform forecasting simulations and analysis of possible energy scenarios.
Propose regulation strategies that favor the transition towards a model dominated by renewable energies.

syllabus_topics: Historical perspective of the energy sector. Energy demand in Spain.
Energy demand forecasting and cost and investment analysis.
International trade of oil and gas.
The Iberian electricity market. Competition and integration of renewable energies.
Environmental determinants, regulation strategies, and emissions trading.

assessment_methods.method: Practical work (T1): individual work on electricity demand forecasting in Spain for specific dates.
Practical work (T2): pair work on characteristics and costs of each electricity generation technology and its past and future evolution worldwide.

Practical work (T3): pair work on income to be received by generation plants of different technologies under MIBEL price scenarios in different periods of the year, including cases with battery management.
Practical work (T4): pair work on the recent evolution of various international energy markets, with future forecasts.
Final exam (E), with questions and exercises on all course content.

assessment_rules: The final grade (NF) in the ordinary call is calculated as: NF = 0.125 * (T1 + T2 + T3 + T4) + 0.5 * E, where the grades for each practical work and the final exam are out of 10 points. There are no minimum grades for any component. For students with differentiated evaluation, the grade for the call will be the final exam grade (E). For the extraordinary call, the grades for practical work T1, T2, T3, and T4 completed during the course will be retained, applying the same criteria as in the ordinary call.
bibliography: Presentations by the professor, exercises, and work scripts on case studies.
Public reports from national and international energy sector agencies, organizations, and companies.
Links to conferences, webinars, and technical events of interest.
